documents: Shan et al. 2023, Geophysical Prospecting 71:102-113, published paper (PDF)

entry.evidence: However, the separated pure P-wave of this approach is coupled with undesired S-wave in anisotropic media called S-wave artefacts.

steps.action: Pose the problem from the literature: the classic acoustic approximation for anisotropic media leaves S-wave artefacts and is unstable when delta > epsilon, so a pure P-wave equation for HTI media is needed.
steps.quote: the effect of S-wave in the previous pseudo-acoustic expression cannot be entirely eliminated by setting S-wave vertical phase velocity to zero

steps.action: Adopt two published tools: the new acoustic approximation of Xu, Stovas and co-authors (2020) for VTI media, and the auxiliary differential operator of Xu and Zhou (2014, 2015).
steps.quote: following the method of the new acoustic approximation

steps.action: Derive the HTI Christoffel equation and phase velocities, then set the SV-wave phase velocity to zero to express the axial S-wave velocity as a function of direction, giving a reformulated pure P-wave phase velocity (Eq. 8).
steps.quote: the axial S-wave phase velocity can be expressed as a function related to propagation directions

steps.action: Check the approximate phase velocity against the exact phase velocities at three azimuths for one HTI model (Figure 1), and compute the relative error versus dip angle (Figure 2).
steps.quote: the calculation results have high accuracy with relative errors of less than 0.13%

steps.action: Convert the phase velocity to slowness form, introduce the vertical S-wave expression as an auxiliary operator S, and derive a second-order time-domain pure P-wave equation (Eq. 14), with S computed from the wavefield gradient.
steps.quote: set the expression of vertical S-wave velocity as an auxiliary differential operator

steps.action: Build a 10th-order space, 2nd-order time finite-difference scheme, derive its stability condition by plane-wave analysis, and add split PML boundary conditions.
steps.quote: Equation (20) shows the stability condition of the derived finite-difference scheme.

steps.action: Design three kinds of density-normalized synthetic test models (homogeneous, two-layered, BP 2007 benchmark section) for finite-difference simulation.
steps.quote: we design three kinds of models for the numerical simulation

steps.action: Simulate two homogeneous models (epsilon > delta and delta > epsilon) in 2D and 3D and compare the snapshots with the coupled pseudo-acoustic equation of Zhou et al. (2006) (Figures 3-5).
steps.quote: the equation proposed in this paper can stably simulate the propagation of pure P-wave, whereas another is unstable in the same case

steps.action: Simulate a two-layered model with strongly varying anisotropy to test stability at the interface, and extract synthetic records at three azimuths (Figures 6-8).
steps.quote: To test the stability of wave propagation at the interface, a two-layered model is designed as the second example.

steps.action: Apply the equation to part of the BP 2007 anisotropic benchmark in 2D: wavefield snapshot, synthetic record and reverse time migration image (Figures 9-12).
steps.quote: the pure P-waveform via the derived equation can stably simulate the wavefield in the complex anisotropic model

steps.action: Keep the claim that the second-order pure P-wave equation is free of S-wave artefacts and simulates HTI P-waves stably and accurately, and assert without testing that it extends to other anisotropic media.
steps.quote: the proposed P-wave equation can stably simulate the Pwaveform in HTI media with high accuracy

tree.answer: S-wave artefacts and instability in pseudo-acoustic anisotropic modelling (known from literature)
No; studied only through synthetic simulation
Derive an artefact-free, stable, second-order pure P-wave equation for HTI media
Coupled pseudo-acoustic equation (Zhou et al. 2006); cubic new acoustic approximation (Xu et al. 2020)
Coupled equation predicts artefacts and instability when delta > epsilon; new equation predicts neither
Conditions set: synthetic models with chosen parameters
Yes, qualitatively, across homogeneous, layered and BP 2007 models
Kept: method characterized as stable and accurate

end.claim: The derived second-order pure P-wave equation for HTI media has no S-wave artefacts and stably simulates P-waves with high accuracy.

decisive_move.sentence: Introducing the direction-dependent vertical S-wave velocity as an auxiliary operator S reduces the cubic pure P-wave relation to a second-order equation (Eq. 14) without redundant solutions.

gates.evidence: No data were acquired. The intent to remove artefacts and instability directed the choice of test models (epsilon > delta and delta > epsilon, p. 111). The phase-velocity approximation faced a quantitative test against the exact equation (relative error < 0.13%, p. 105). The wavefield tests are visual judgements without a stated failure criterion. Nothing was fixed in advance.

imports.item: High-order finite-difference scheme and plane-wave (von Neumann type) stability analysis

novelty_claims.quote: we propose a pure P-wave equation for HTI media
Finally, an improved pure P-wave equation with a second-order differential form is deduced.

limits: PDF only; no review file, so no review sequence. No code or data released ('available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request', p. 112). The only quantitative accuracy check concerns the phase-velocity formula (Eq. 8). The wavefield simulations of Eq. 14 are judged visually, with no error measure against elastic or exact modelling. The RTM image is not compared with a reference image. Extension to TTI and orthorhombic media is asserted but not tested. Computational cost is mentioned but not measured. Internal inconsistencies (inference: labelling errors): the text calls model 2 'epsilon > delta' although it sets epsilon = 0.1 and delta = 0.2; Figure 3 cites Equation (11) for the wave equation; the error check names 'exact Equation (7)' where Eq. 6 is meant. Composition none_fits: this is a method-derivation-then-verification walk. The question precedes the capability and no phenomenon is established, so capability_first does not fit, and there is no crucial test among rivals. Sub-claims: phase-velocity accuracy, relative error < 0.13% for one parameter set (estimate_with_resolution, single model); absence of artefacts and stability (capability_characterized, visual); generality to other anisotropic media (none).

disagreements.support: Cites the literature showing residual S-wave artefacts and instability when delta > epsilon; its own Figure 3 shows the artefacts in the coupled equation.
disagreements.quote: The two sets of conjugate solutions for acoustic approximation wave equation result in the instability of numerical simulation in the condition of 𝛿>𝜀

disagreements.target: Phase velocity approximation methods (Fowler 2003; Pestana et al. 2011; Schleicher & Costa 2016 and others)
disagreements.support: Argument only: the square-root approximation limits accuracy; not tested here.
disagreements.quote: whereas the corresponding assumption limits the simulation accuracy of the simplified equation

disagreements.target: New acoustic approximation ( [...] , Stovas & Mikada 2020; Xu, Stovas, Alkhalifah et al. 2020)
disagreements.support: Points out the cubic form with redundant roots and offers a second-order reformulation; no direct numerical comparison.
disagreements.quote: However, the form of this new acoustic approximation is quite complicated.

disagreements.support: Side-by-side snapshots in homogeneous models show artefacts in model 1 and instability in model 2 for the coupled equation, but not for the new equation.
disagreements.quote: whereas another is unstable in the same case

alternatives_considered.chosen: Reconstruct Eq. 6 and substitute Eq. 7 to get a simplified pure P-wave phase velocity (Eq. 8)
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Direct substitution of the axial S-wave velocity into the P-wave phase velocity formula, following Xu et al. (2020)
alternatives_considered.reason: The exact solution is cubic with two redundant solutions, and the complicated expression makes numerical simulation harder

alternatives_considered.alternatives: Directly solving the cubic equation for p_z
alternatives_considered.reason: To avoid directly solving the cubic equation

alternatives_considered.chosen: New acoustic approximation combined with an auxiliary operator
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Phase velocity (square-root) approximation methods; auxiliary operator applied to the classic acoustic approximation
alternatives_considered.reason: The square-root approximation limits accuracy; the classic approximation leaves S-wave artefacts
